Buoy 10 salmon fishing: season and charter checklist

Buoy 10 salmon fishing starts with the rule for your date. For November 1–December 31, 2026, ODFW allows two adult hatchery coho or hatchery steelhead combined from Buoy 10 to Bonneville Dam; release all Chinook. Check the latest notice, barbless hooks, launch and weather plan before you book.[1] [2]

01

What does Buoy 10 mean?

Buoy 10 names the salmon fishery where the Columbia meets the Pacific. It is not a label for every salmon trip on the river. Ask the captain which launch and estuary area the trip uses, and whether an ocean crossing is part of the plan.

Locally, kings are Chinook and silvers are coho. Use the standard species name when you check the regulation notice. A photograph of a salmon does not tell you whether that fish can be retained on your date.[3]

02

2026 Buoy 10 season: dates, limits and hook rules

Checked November 17, 2026. The table covers the current late-season notice, not the summer opening. ODFW lists November 1–December 31 for the reach from Buoy 10 upstream to Bonneville Dam.

Summer rules changed during the run. WDFW’s August 21 update kept Chinook retention hatchery-only through September 2. Use the notice for your actual date, not an earlier season chart.[1] [2] [4]

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

Late-2026 checkRule or next step
Dates and reachNovember 1–December 31; Buoy 10 upstream to Bonneville Dam.
Adult daily limitTwo hatchery coho/steelhead combined.
ChinookRelease all Chinook.
HooksBarbless hooks for salmon and steelhead.
Before departureRead the latest agency notice; all other permanent rules still apply.
03

Is Buoy 10 barbless hook fishing?

Yes. Oregon’s 2026 rules require barbless hooks for salmon, steelhead, sturgeon and trout in the mainstem Columbia from Buoy 10 to the Oregon–Washington border above McNary Dam. Check the specific gear rules for the fish you target.[2]

04

How do tide and wind change the plan?

ODFW warns that an ebb tide with a west wind can make the Buoy 10 area rough, especially in the shipping channel below the Astoria–Megler Bridge. It advises avoiding Clatsop Spit and the Astoria shipping channel during tide runout. Wear a life jacket.

The table turns those warnings into questions for your trip. It is not a navigation plan or a set of safe wind limits. A favorable tide for fishing does not establish suitable boating conditions.[3]

A long run from the launchWhere can we return if conditions change?Keep the return journey in the plan.
Possible ocean crossingDoes the trip include crossing the bar?Evaluate that separately from an estuary-only outing.
05

What should a beginner know about the tackle?

Ask which trolling system the crew will use and what the angler does after a bite. Get a demonstration while the boat is still quiet. Learn where to stand, where spare rods go and who handles the landing net.

Bring personal rods only after the captain approves the complete setup. Ask for the rod, reel, line and terminal tackle as one system. A familiar freshwater outfit may not be the one the crew wants alongside its other trolling rods.

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

Ask aboutWhy it helps

Rod-holder and bite procedureKnow when to act and when to wait.

Fish identification and releaseFollow the rule that applies that day.
06

What does a guided Buoy 10 day include?

Ask for a written list of what the charter supplies. A guided day can use the crew’s trolling setup, but rods, bait, fish handling, food and licence arrangements belong in the operator’s own terms. Do not assume they come with every booking.

Compare the launch, time aboard, boat run and fishing time separately. Ask whether the plan stays in the estuary or crosses the bar. Then compare shelter, seating and cancellation terms. These questions help you choose a trip that fits your group.

  • ✓Record the launch and meeting address.
  • ✓Confirm whether the advertised hours include the boat run.
  • ✓Ask about seating, shelter and toilet access.
  • ✓Confirm who supplies food, water and ice.
  • ✓Ask how any legal retained catch is handled after the trip.
  • ✓Get the cancellation terms before a deposit.

A few good questions

Before you head out

Is Buoy 10 the same as ocean salmon fishing?

No. This page concerns the Columbia estuary fishery. Ask separately whether a proposed trip crosses the Columbia River bar.

Does the general August season advice establish an opening?

No. Check the current Columbia regulations and in-season notice for the exact date and area.

What are kings and silvers?

Kings means Chinook salmon; silvers means coho salmon. Use the standard names when checking retention rules.

Is an ebb tide always a good time to go?

No. ODFW warns that an ebb tide with west wind can produce rough conditions. The boating decision comes before the fishing opportunity.

Should a beginner bring a trolling rod?

Ask first. A supplied setup can avoid a mismatch with the crew’s method. Bring your own only after the captain approves it.

Does a charter price include a fishing licence?

Do not assume so. Ask the operator which licence and endorsements each angler needs for the intended water.

Are barbless hooks required at Buoy 10?

Yes, for salmon and steelhead. Check the current Columbia River rules and any in-season changes before departure.
